name: Methodist renewal movement
description: Methodism began as a renewal movement within the Church of England in the 18th century.
narrative: Methodism began as a renewal movement within the Church of England in the 18th century. John and Charles Wesley worked within the Church of England while organizing societies and preaching beyond ordinary parish settings. Regular meetings, lay leadership, and hymns helped participants sustain a demanding devotional life. John Wesley’s 1738 assurance experience is a major milestone, not the only possible beginning of Methodism. Separate Methodist institutions developed gradually; the movement should not simply be treated as dissolved when new churches emerged.

key_figures.name: John Wesley
key_figures.summary: An Anglican minister and organizer of Methodist societies who linked the message of grace to disciplined discipleship and growth in love.

key_figures.name: Charles Wesley
key_figures.summary: An Anglican minister and prolific hymn writer whose songs taught Methodist theology and helped sustain its devotional and congregational life.

name: American Methodist organization
description: Methodist Episcopal Church formed in 1784 as American Methodism organized separately from the Church of England.
narrative: Methodist Episcopal Church formed in 1784 as American Methodism organized separately from the Church of England. The American Revolution disrupted Anglican structures that had served Methodist societies. Wesley commissioned Thomas Coke, and the Christmas Conference in Baltimore organized the Methodist Episcopal Church in 1784 with Francis Asbury as a central leader. An itinerant ministry helped it expand widely. Slavery, authority, and representation later generated divisions; northern and southern branches participated in the 1939 Methodist reunion.
